record.original_question: For the same generic single-input time-optimal control problem qdot = f(q) + u g(q) with |u| ≤ 1 on a 3-dimensional manifold, let sw(q) denote the smallest local uniform bound on the number of switching points of sufficiently short time-optimal trajectories near q, with sw(q) = ∞ if arbitrarily close optimal trajectories can have infinitely many switching points. Is sw(q) finite for every point q in M?

evidence.quote: We do not know if sw(q) < ∞ for any q ∈ M.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a generic single-input control-affine system on a smooth 3-dimensional manifold $M$ of the form
$$\dot q = f(q) + u\, g(q), \qquad |u(t)| \le 1,$$
where $f, g$ are smooth vector fields on $M$ and admissible controls are measurable functions with values in $[-1,1]$. A trajectory is called time-optimal if it minimizes the time needed to steer between its endpoints among all admissible trajectories with the same endpoints. A switching point of an admissible bang-bang trajectory is a time at which the control $u(t)$ changes sign.

For each point $q \in M$, define $\mathrm{sw}(q)$ to be the smallest nonnegative integer $N$ with the following property: there exist a neighborhood $U$ of $q$ and a time $T>0$ such that every time-optimal trajectory $\gamma:[0,t_\gamma]\to M$ contained in $U$ with $t_\gamma \le T$ has at most $N$ switching points. Set $\mathrm{sw}(q) = \infty$ if no such finite $N$ exists, i.e., if there exist time-optimal trajectories arbitrarily close to $q$, of arbitrarily short duration, having arbitrarily many switching points.

Question: For a generic pair $(f,g)$, is $\mathrm{sw}(q) < \infty$ for every $q \in M$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether a uniform local bound on the number of switching points exists for time-optimal trajectories of generic single-input control-affine systems on 3-dimensional manifolds appears to remain open. Related work by Agrachev–Sigalotti and Agrachev–Biolo establishes finite switching bounds in regular regions and under specific Lie-bracket conditions, but a finite bound at every point — including a "bad" lower-dimensional subset — has not been established. No source found that resolves the question in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Switching in Time-Optimal Problem: the 3D Case with 2D Control (Agrachev-Biolo)
status_evidence.snippet: At most 4 switchings in regular regions; the existence of a bound on the number of switchings at points of a 'bad' 1-dimensional subset remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Related results give bounds in regular regions but the general finiteness question is left open.

status_evidence.title: Regularity properties of optimal trajectories of single-input control systems in dimension three
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes structure of time-optimal controls on 3-manifolds with single input, obtaining bang-bang/singular concatenations under Lie bracket genericity.
status_evidence.claim: Local structure results exist but do not uniformly bound the number of switchings near every point.
